assessment: The learner cites 14,045 (May), 13,992 (Jun), 13,875 (Jul), 12,730 (Aug) as three straight declines. The figures are accurate against the table, but the conclusion is wrong. The round's concept is separating a recurring seasonal dip from a trend change, and the visible text shows August fell 8.4% in 2025 and 8.3% in 2026, and that YoY growth stayed about 35%, in line with the 32-37% seen before May. Measuring from the May launch peak ignores both the seasonality and the launch spike that faded. The learner never compares to last year, so the evidence does not separate seasonal dip from slowdown. answer_sound is false because it concludes a real slowdown; why_sound is false as a result.
